headline: India Launches World's Largest Solar Power Grid in Rajasthan Desert
body: India has officially inaugurated the world's largest solar power installation spanning 56,000 acres in the Thar Desert. The project, developed in partnership with multiple global energy firms, will generate 30 gigawatts of clean electricity — enough to power 30 million homes. Prime Minister Modi called it a historic leap toward India's 2070 net-zero target. The project employed over 200,000 workers during construction and is expected to reduce carbon emissions by 60 million tonnes annually.

headline: ISRO Successfully Tests Reusable Launch Vehicle for Commercial Missions
body: The Indian Space Research Organisation achieved a landmark milestone as its Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV) completed its third consecutive successful landing. The technology, years in development, will drastically cut satellite launch costs by up to 80%. ISRO Chairman S. Somanath announced commercial bookings are now open, with 14 international clients already signed. This positions India as a major player in the global commercial space economy.

headline: India vs Australia: Test Series Finale Ends in Historic Draw at MCG
body: The fifth and final Test between India and Australia ended in a gripping draw at Melbourne Cricket Ground, with India retaining the Border-Gavaskar Trophy 2-1. Virat Kohli scored a masterful 180* to save the match on day five, while Jasprit Bumrah claimed his 300th Test wicket. The series drew a combined television audience of 800 million across both countries — the most watched cricket series in history.

headline: Parliament Passes Historic Data Protection Bill with Strong Privacy Safeguards
body: Both houses of the Indian Parliament have unanimously passed the Digital Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Bill, bringing sweeping changes to how tech companies handle citizen data. The bill mandates data localization for sensitive categories, grants users the right to erasure, and levies fines up to ₹500 crore for breaches. Opposition leaders praised the cross-party consensus while privacy advocates called it a step in the right direction, though some concerns remain around government exemptions.

headline: Bollywood's Biggest Collaboration: 5 A-Listers Unite for Epic Historical Drama
body: In an unprecedented move for Hindi cinema, Shah Rukh Khan, Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone, Alia Bhatt, and Hrithik Roshan have confirmed roles in a single mega-budget production titled 'Mahabharata — The Beginning'. Director SS Rajamouli will helm the ₹2,000 crore project, shooting across 12 countries over three years. The announcement broke social media records with 50 million mentions in 24 hours, making it the most anticipated Indian film ever.

headline: Reliance Jio Launches 6G Trials in Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore
body: Reliance Jio has begun 6G network trials across three major Indian cities, achieving download speeds of 1 terabit per second in controlled environments. The company has partnered with Nokia, Ericsson, and Samsung for the rollout, investing ₹1.5 lakh crore over five years. The commercial 6G launch is targeted for 2028, which would make India among the world's first countries with nationwide next-gen connectivity.

headline: Budget 2025: Middle Class Tax Relief, Infrastructure Boom Announced
body: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2025 with zero income tax for earnings up to ₹12 lakh, a record ₹15 lakh crore capital expenditure on infrastructure, and a ₹2 lakh crore agriculture fund. The budget also allocates ₹50,000 crore for AI and semiconductor research. Markets responded positively with the Sensex surging 2,400 points. Economists broadly praised the fiscal discipline while maintaining welfare spending.

headline: IPL 2025: Mumbai Indians Break Record with 7th Championship Title
body: Mumbai Indians clinched their record-breaking seventh IPL title at a packed Wankhede Stadium, defeating Royal Challengers Bengaluru by 8 wickets in a rain-affected final. Rohit Sharma top-scored with 94 off 52 balls, while young sensation Tilak Varma was adjudged Player of the Tournament. The final drew a staggering 650 million viewers globally, making it the most watched T20 match in cricket history.

headline: India's UPI Goes Global: Now Accepted in 50 Countries
body: The National Payments Corporation of India announced that UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is now operational in 50 countries following new agreements with Japan, South Korea, and 12 European nations. The platform processes over $300 billion in transactions monthly domestically. International UPI adoption is expected to generate $5 billion in annual foreign exchange earnings by 2027, fundamentally reshaping global digital payments.

headline: Neeraj Chopra Wins Diamond League Title with 93.2m World Record Throw
body: Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra shattered the javelin world record with a stunning 93.2-metre throw at the Doha Diamond League, becoming the first Asian athlete to hold the world record in the event. The 27-year-old from Panipat dedicated the throw to India on the eve of its National Sports Day. PM Modi personally called to congratulate him; the hashtag NeerajChopra trended globally with over 40 million tweets.

headline: Startup India: 10 Indian Unicorns Cross $1 Billion Valuation in a Single Month
body: March 2025 became India's most prolific startup month, with ten companies achieving unicorn status in a single calendar month — a global record. Sectors represented include agritech, deeptech, edtech, and climate-fintech. Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi-NCR collectively account for 8 of the 10. Total startup funding in India crossed $40 billion for the fiscal year, making it the world's third-largest startup ecosystem behind the US and China.

headline: AIIMS Develops AI Diagnostic Tool That Detects 50 Diseases from a Blood Drop
body: Researchers at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences have unveiled an AI-powered microfluidic device capable of diagnosing 50 diseases — including early-stage cancers, tuberculosis, and dengue — from a single drop of blood in under 15 minutes. The device costs ₹500 per test versus thousands for conventional diagnostics. WHO has expressed interest in deploying it across Sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. Mass production is expected to begin by Q4 2025.
